industry.why: Neutral, carried. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): Jefferies' desk (17 Oct) names utilities with staples as 'pricing-power defensives' and utilities led the US week, which is the defensive case; against it, utilities are the classic bond proxy, the Fed hikes in December and no European power price was read. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: D now, D prior. Integrated generators and regulated networks stay C at sector level, renewable generators D.

sector.key: E.3. Utilities - renewable generators and developers
sector.why: Underweight, from Neutral, correcting a relabel. The C on this row was written for the old 'Water and other non-power' Sector; the row now holds the renewable generators and developers, the debt-funded, longest-duration, most capex-dependent end of utilities, which is exactly the case the prior E.2 reason described and the regime punishes. Component 1 regime, 16-Oct-26 (a discount-rate shock with the first credit crack inside the artificial intelligence chain: United States core inflation re-accelerating on energy, the Fed and Bank of England hikes pulled forward, the US 10-year about 5.1%, the US joined the sell-off and Asia is in washout, defensives bid for four weeks in Europe, European breadth off its three-year lows but in the bottom quarter, the consumer forecast to weaken into winter; sources present 2026-W42): higher real yields are the direct headwind to a build-out financed at the margin, and no non-AI demand theme (electrification included) was spoken to by any source this week. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-16 against 2026-08-14, not week on week: F now, F prior, agrees. Counter-case: power is a political constraint on data centres and the energy shock lifts power prices for every generator; thirteen stocks, none in the MI Pool. Back to C if the Fed path is marked down and the sector's relative strength leaves F.

geography.why: Neutral, carried. No source spoke to Poland this week; Goldman's note (22 Oct) that emerging-market sovereign spreads are widening with US rate volatility is general, not Polish, and the condition for D (a source reading Polish spreads wider, or a third memo naming the sovereign) is not met; no memo carried a congruence line this week. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43). Twelve of the 149 Pool stocks are Polish, seven of them banks, so this is still the country row most likely to move. Relative strength is not graded by country.
